adc-dac-001.question: How many output levels can an 8-bit AD converter represent?
adc-dac-001.explanation: An N-bit converter can represent 2 to the power N levels. For 8 bits, that is 2⁸ = 256 levels. 1024 levels corresponds to 10 bits. Each additional bit doubles the number of levels, allowing finer voltage differences to be distinguished.

adc-dac-002.question: What sampling frequency is needed to sample an analog signal containing components up to 20 kHz without aliasing?
adc-dac-002.explanation: By the sampling theorem, the original signal can be reconstructed if it is sampled at more than twice its highest frequency. Twice 20 kHz is 40 kHz. The 44.1 kHz sampling frequency of music CDs was chosen based on the upper limit of human hearing, about 20 kHz.

adc-dac-003.question: Which is a characteristic of a flash AD converter?
choices: It converts in one step using many comparators in parallel, so it is fast, but circuit size grows rapidly with resolution
It compares one bit at a time, so it is slow but small
It integrates the input voltage for a long time, so it is accurate but slow
adc-dac-003.explanation: A flash converter compares the input voltage with reference voltages using 2ᴺ−1 comparators at once, so conversion finishes in a single comparison, making it the fastest architecture. In return, N bits require 2ᴺ−1 comparators, so area and power increase sharply as resolution increases.

adc-dac-004.question: Which correctly describes the operation of a successive-approximation (SAR) AD converter?
choices: It integrates the input voltage for a fixed time and measures the discharge time
Starting from the most significant bit, it compares the input voltage with the output of an internal DAC and decides one bit at a time
It achieves high resolution through oversampling and noise shaping
adc-dac-004.explanation: A successive-approximation converter asks, starting from the most significant bit, whether the input is larger than the internal DAC output, deciding one bit at a time like a binary search. An N-bit conversion needs N comparisons. Its good balance of speed, accuracy and power makes it widely used, for example in microcontroller ADCs. Measuring by integration is the dual-slope type, and oversampling is used by the delta-sigma type.

adc-dac-005.question: What is the maximum quantization error of an ideal AD converter? (LSB: the voltage corresponding to one least significant bit)
adc-dac-005.explanation: Because a continuous analog value is rounded to steps of a fixed width (1 LSB), conversion always introduces error. This quantization error is at most ±1/2 LSB in an ideal ADC. More bits make 1 LSB smaller and reduce quantization error.

adc-dac-006.question: Which is a characteristic of a delta-sigma (ΔΣ) AD converter?
choices: It readily achieves high resolution through oversampling and noise shaping
It is the fastest of all architectures
It requires 2ᴺ−1 comparators for N-bit conversion
adc-dac-006.explanation: A delta-sigma converter samples at a frequency far higher than the signal band (oversampling), pushes quantization noise to high frequencies (noise shaping), and removes it with a digital filter. Because it achieves high resolution at low frequencies, it is used in audio and measurement applications.

adc-dac-007.question: For a 10-bit AD converter with a full-scale input of 1.024 V, what voltage corresponds to 1 LSB?
adc-dac-007.explanation: Ten bits give 2¹⁰ = 1024 levels, so 1 LSB = 1.024 V ÷ 1024 = 1 mV. With 12-bit resolution and the same full scale, 1 LSB would be 0.25 mV.

adc-dac-008.question: What type of filter is used as the anti-aliasing filter placed before an AD converter?
adc-dac-008.explanation: If components above half the sampling frequency (the Nyquist frequency) reach the ADC, they fold back into false low-frequency signals. To prevent this, a low-pass filter is placed before the ADC to remove components above the Nyquist frequency.

adc-dac-009.question: Which is a characteristic of an R-2R ladder DA converter?
choices: It can be built with only two resistor values (R and 2R), so few resistor values are needed
It is built only from capacitors
adc-dac-009.explanation: An R-2R ladder combines resistors R and 2R in a ladder to produce currents or voltages weighted according to each bit. Even as the number of bits increases, only two resistor values are needed, and it is easy to match the accuracy of resistor ratios.

adc-dac-010.question: What is the role of a sample-and-hold circuit placed before an AD converter?
choices: To hold the input voltage constant while AD conversion is performed
adc-dac-010.explanation: AD conversion takes a certain amount of time, and if the input voltage changes during that time, it cannot be converted correctly. A sample-and-hold circuit captures the input voltage at one instant on a capacitor and holds it until conversion is complete. It is essential in successive-approximation ADCs and others.

adc-dac-011.question: Which is the approximate formula for the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of an ideal N-bit AD converter, set by quantization noise? (For a full-scale sine-wave input)
adc-dac-011.explanation: For an ideal ADC, SNR ≈ 6.02N + 1.76 dB, improving by about 6 dB for each additional bit. For example, 12 bits give about 74 dB. Real ADCs fall short of this because of thermal noise, distortion and other factors.

adc-dac-012.question: Which is a characteristic of the dual-slope AD converter often used in digital multimeters?
choices: It is the fastest because it uses many comparators
It is slow but accurate, and integration makes it resistant to noise
adc-dac-012.explanation: A dual-slope converter integrates the input voltage for a fixed time, then integrates the reference voltage in the opposite direction and counts the time until it returns to zero. Component value errors cancel out and noise is averaged by integration, so it is highly accurate. Because conversion takes time, it is used in slow applications such as measuring instruments.

adc-dac-013.question: Which correctly describes the differential nonlinearity (DNL) of an AD converter?
choices: Error in the slope (gain) of the overall transfer characteristic
Deviation of the width (step size) between adjacent codes from the ideal 1 LSB
Deviation of the output when the input is 0
adc-dac-013.explanation: DNL indicates how much the input voltage width corresponding to each output code deviates from the ideal 1 LSB. Deviation of the overall transfer characteristic from the ideal straight line is integral nonlinearity (INL), and the output deviation at zero input is offset error.

adc-dac-014.question: What is the AD converter defect called in which a certain output code never appears no matter how the input changes?
adc-dac-014.explanation: A code with a DNL of −1 LSB or less has no corresponding input width and never appears at the output. This is a missing code. In control systems, non-monotonic outputs are a problem, so the absence of missing codes is sometimes guaranteed in the specifications.

adc-dac-015.question: Which is a characteristic of the current-steering architecture often used in high-speed DA converters?
choices: It is slow because it integrates the input for a long time
It produces the output by slowly discharging a capacitor
It produces the output by switching where the currents of many current sources go, so it suits high-speed operation
adc-dac-015.explanation: A current-steering DAC has many current sources and, according to the digital input, switches each current to either the output or a dummy path, forming the output from the summed current. Because the current sources keep running and only their destination switches, it is fast and is used in high-speed DACs for communication equipment.

adc-dac-016.question: Which metric converts the performance of a real AD converter, including noise and distortion, into the bit count of an ideal ADC?
adc-dac-016.explanation: ENOB (effective number of bits) is calculated from the measured SINAD (signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio) as ENOB = (SINAD − 1.76) / 6.02. Even a 12-bit ADC may have an ENOB of about 10 bits because of noise and distortion, so ENOB is used to compare real-world performance.

adc-dac-017.question: Which AD converter splits conversion into several stages processed like an assembly line, combining high speed with medium to high resolution?
adc-dac-017.explanation: A pipeline ADC converts a few bits in each stage, amplifies the remaining error (residue) and passes it to the next stage. Because each stage processes a different sample in parallel, it combines conversion rates of tens to hundreds of MS/s with resolutions of about 10 to 14 bits, and is used in communications and video.

adc-dac-018.question: With simple oversampling and no noise shaping, how much does quantization noise improve when the sampling frequency is quadrupled?
adc-dac-018.explanation: The total quantization noise is fixed, so raising the sampling frequency spreads it thinly over a wider frequency range. In-band noise decreases by 10 log₁₀(4) ≈ 6 dB, an improvement of about 1 bit. Delta-sigma converters combine this with noise shaping to achieve much larger improvements.

adc-dac-019.question: Why does timing fluctuation (jitter) of the sampling clock become a problem when converting high-frequency signals?
choices: Because errors occur only for DC signals
Because the faster the signal changes, the larger the voltage error caused by a tiny shift in sampling time
adc-dac-019.explanation: If the sampling instant shifts by Δt, an error occurs equal to how much the signal changed during that time. The higher the signal frequency, the steeper its slope, so the same jitter produces a larger error and degrades SNR. High-speed, high-resolution ADCs need low-jitter clocks.

adc-dac-020.question: When a microcontroller produces an analog voltage by passing a PWM signal through a low-pass filter, what determines the output voltage?
choices: The duty cycle of the pulses (the fraction of each period that is on)
The memory capacity of the microcontroller
adc-dac-020.explanation: When a PWM signal is averaged by a low-pass filter, the output voltage is amplitude × duty cycle. For example, 5 V pulses with a 40% duty cycle give about 2 V. Analog voltages can be produced easily without a dedicated DAC, but ripple remains, so accuracy and speed are limited.

adc-dac-021.question: What does 'MS/s (MSPS)', used to express the conversion speed of an AD converter, mean?
choices: How many million times per second it can sample (convert)
The number of milliseconds per conversion
adc-dac-021.explanation: MS/s stands for mega samples per second and indicates how many million times per second the converter can sample and convert. For example, a 100 MS/s ADC converts 100 million times per second. By the sampling theorem, the highest signal frequency it can handle is half that.

adc-dac-022.question: In the transfer characteristic of an AD converter, what is the error called when the output deviates from 0 at zero input?
adc-dac-022.explanation: Offset error is a parallel shift of the whole transfer characteristic, appearing as an output deviation at zero input. Error in the slope is called gain error. Both can usually be corrected by calibration.

adc-dac-023.question: What is an advantage of using a differential input for an AD converter?
choices: Common-mode noise is easily canceled, and a larger signal swing can be handled
adc-dac-023.explanation: With a differential input, the voltage difference between two signal lines is converted, so noise appearing equally on both (common-mode noise) cancels. It also handles twice the swing of a single-ended input at the same supply voltage, making it easier to raise SNR. Most high-performance ADCs use differential inputs.

adc-dac-024.question: In a delta-sigma AD converter, which digital circuit converts the fast, coarse quantized output into high-resolution data at a lower sampling rate?
adc-dac-024.explanation: A delta-sigma modulator outputs a coarse signal, such as 1 bit, at a high sampling rate. The decimation filter averages that output with a digital low-pass filter, removing the quantization noise pushed to high frequencies, and lowers the sampling rate while producing high-resolution data.

adc-dac-025.question: What is the brief spike-like error that appears at the output of a DA converter at the moment the input code changes?
adc-dac-025.explanation: A glitch is a temporary disturbance of the output caused, for example, by slight timing differences between switches when several bits change at once. It tends to be largest near mid-scale codes where many bits change together (for example, from 0111… to 1000…), and it affects the performance of high-speed DACs.

adc-dac-026.question: Which architecture runs several AD converters alternately with slightly staggered timing to achieve a high overall sampling rate?
adc-dac-026.explanation: In a time-interleaved converter, for example, four ADCs are staggered by a quarter period to achieve four times the sampling rate of one ADC. Mismatches in offset, gain and timing between the ADCs create spurs (unwanted signal components), so calibration techniques are important.

adc-dac-027.question: What is the main reason for placing a driver circuit, such as an op-amp, in front of a successive-approximation AD converter?
choices: To change the color of the input signal
To charge the ADC's internal sampling capacitor quickly and capture the input voltage accurately
To reduce the ADC's power consumption to zero
adc-dac-027.explanation: A successive-approximation ADC connects its internal capacitor to the input at the sampling instant. If the source impedance is high, the capacitor does not charge in the short time available and the voltage is not captured accurately. A driver with low output impedance charges the capacitor quickly and accurately.

adc-dac-028.question: Which architecture is used as the internal DAC in many successive-approximation AD converters?
choices: A capacitor array using capacitance ratios (charge redistribution)
adc-dac-028.explanation: Many SAR ADCs use an array of binary-weighted capacitors and generate the comparison voltage by switching the capacitors to redistribute charge. The capacitor array can also serve as the sampling capacitor and draws no static current, allowing low power consumption.

adc-dac-029.question: Which is a characteristic of a resistor-string DAC, which connects many resistors in series?
choices: Its output is structurally guaranteed to change monotonically with the input code
It uses only two resistor values
adc-dac-029.explanation: A resistor-string DAC selects, with switches, the tap of the series resistor chain that corresponds to the input code. When the code increases by 1, the next higher tap is always selected, so the output always increases monotonically. As bits increase, the number of resistors and switches grows to 2ⁿ.

adc-dac-030.question: Which AD converter architecture is classified as oversampling?
adc-dac-030.explanation: ADCs are divided into Nyquist-rate types that sample at about twice the Nyquist frequency (flash, successive approximation, pipeline and others) and oversampling types that sample at much higher rates. The delta-sigma converter is the representative oversampling type.
